13 A uniform square sign of weight 40 N is suspended vertically from its top edge by a horizontal
hinge, as shown.
front view

hinge
sign
sign
0.80 m
0.80 m
The hinge is not frictionless. When the sign is displaced from the vertical by an external force and
then released, it does not return to the vertical position.
The maximum torque exerted by the hinge on the sign is 6.0 N m. The sign is displaced by 90 so
that it is horizontal and then gradually released.
At which angle to the vertical does the sign hang after release?
A
11
B
22
C
68
D
79

hints: Notice the uniform $0.80 \text{ m}$ square sign pivots at its top edge, so its $40 \text{ N}$ weight acts at the centre, $0.40 \text{ m}$ from the hinge.
The turning effect of the weight about the hinge depends on the angle to the vertical as $W \times 0.40 \sin\theta$, which is maximum when horizontal and zero when vertical.
Set that weight torque equal to the maximum $6.0 \text{ N m}$ frictional torque from the hinge and solve for $\sin\theta$, checking whether you need the angle to the vertical or horizontal.
walkthrough: The sign falls from horizontal toward vertical but is held out by friction in the hinge. It stops where the clockwise torque due to weight just equals the maximum anticlockwise torque the hinge can provide, $6.0 \text{ N m}$.
For a uniform sign the centre of mass is at its geometric centre, so the distance from hinge to line of weight is $0.80/2 = 0.40 \text{ m}$ along the sign.
If $\theta$ is the angle to the vertical, the perpendicular distance from the hinge to the weight line is $0.40\sin\theta$. So weight torque is $\tau = W \times 0.40\sin\theta$.
Substitute $W = 40 \text{ N}$ and set equal to hinge torque: $40 \times 0.40 \times \sin\theta = 6.0$. This gives $16\sin\theta = 6.0$.

A.explanation: This uses $0.80 \text{ m}$ as the moment arm, giving $\sin\theta = 0.1875$. The weight acts at the centre, $0.40 \text{ m}$ from the hinge, not at the bottom edge.

B.explanation: Weight torque $40 \times 0.40 \sin\theta$ balances the $6.0 \text{ N m}$ hinge torque, giving $\sin\theta = 0.375$ and $\theta \approx 22^{\circ}$.

C.explanation: This is $90^{\circ}-22^{\circ}$. It correctly finds $\sin\theta = 0.375$ but then gives the angle to the horizontal rather than to the vertical.

D.explanation: This is $90^{\circ}-11^{\circ}$. It both uses the wrong $0.80 \text{ m}$ arm and measures the angle from the horizontal.
